scenario.name: r-cw-delegate-self-continuation
scenario.description: Fires continue_delegate that internally calls continue_work — proves hop-2 woke inside a delegate child session. The delegate dispatches, the child fires its own continue_work, and the hop-2 turn executes.

invocation.promptTemplate: k6 proof R-CW-DELEGATE-SELF nonce {{nonce}}: after arriving, call continue_work(reason="k6-self-continuation-{{nonce}}", delaySeconds=2). After the continue_work tool result reports scheduled, invent a fresh random token of exactly 12 lowercase letters and digits (make it up now; do not copy it from anywhere) and reply exactly CHILD-CW-SCHEDULED {{nonce}} TOKEN <your token>. On hop-2 wake, reply exactly CHILD-HOP2-DONE {{nonce}}. Do not mutate files. Do not post to any channel.

expectedReceipts.name: child-spawned
expectedReceipts.description: Delegate child bound through the child observer: own row spawnedBy = parent and own spawn task carries the nonce, unique; event-path child keys only cross-check (fail closed). The child transcript receipts below need this binding.

expectedReceipts.name: child-continue-work-accepted
expectedReceipts.description: From the CHILD's own chat.history: exactly one nonce-bound continue_work call, its toolResult status "scheduled" (continue-work-tool.ts:86-95), and CHILD-CW-SCHEDULED <nonce> in the same turn. The parent stream cannot see child turns.

expectedReceipts.name: child-hop-2-woke
expectedReceipts.description: From the CHILD's own chat.history: a [continuation:wake] user turn carrying the nonce after the yield (work-dispatch-execution.ts:197-215), and CHILD-HOP2-DONE <nonce> in that wake turn.

expectedReceipts.name: parent-return
expectedReceipts.description: The child's return reached the parent: the parent reproduces, in its own transcript, the token the child minted in its turn-1 reply (CHILD-CW-SCHEDULED <nonce> TOKEN <12 chars>, absent from every harness-sent text) as PARENT-RETURN <nonce> TOKEN <token> (assistant text or heartbeat_respond), in a run other than the dispatch run, after the dispatch run and not before the child minted it. Does not claim that hop-2 OUTPUT reached the parent: only the turn-1 return is delivered.

expectedReceipts.name: tempo-trace-json
expectedReceipts.description: Public-safe Tempo trace JSON (tempo-trace-<id>.json) for the parent's continue_delegate tool → continuation.delegate.dispatch → continuation.delegate.fire topology, collected by collect-continuation-trace.mjs. Required for every continuation row (#600).

expectedReceipts.name: continuation-trace-correlation
expectedReceipts.description: continuation-trace-correlation.json: exactly one Tempo trace matched by the delegate task's reason hash, length, and mode (normal), holding one dispatch, one fire, and the originating continue_delegate tool span on one trace and chain. The scenario publishes the task fingerprint so the trace can also be attributed after the run from public evidence.

review.notes: Delegate self-continuation: detector must ignore [k6-proof-harness] prompt-echo events and count only post-dispatch evidence. PASS-candidate now requires delegate-accepted + child-continue-work-accepted + child-hop-2-woke + parent-return. child-spawned is corroborative only unless a concrete lifecycle signal is available.

census.limits: The census found accepted continuation entry spans carry no origin, session, turn, or run identity and that proof traffic carries no marker, so this row’s trace receipt joins the continue_delegate tool span to continuation.delegate.dispatch and continuation.delegate.fire only by shared trace, causal timing, and the reason fingerprint and mode. The scenario publishes the delegate task fingerprint (reason_hash, reason_length, delegate_mode) in public evidence, so the collector can attribute the parent’s dispatch either in run or afterwards from the public evidence alone. The child’s own continue_work spans have no join to that dispatch and are reviewed by hand.

spans.name: continuation.delegate.dispatch
spans.notes: The parent’s delegate dispatch the collector attributes by the task fingerprint and mode.

spans.name: openclaw.tool.execution
spans.notes: Typed continue_delegate evidence on the parent.

spans.name: continuation.work
spans.notes: The child’s own continue_work entry. Not joinable to the parent dispatch today; reviewed by hand.

attributes.notes: Emitted today and asserted by collect-continuation-trace.mjs. It is the strongest join currently available and it is not an identity.
Accepted entry spans carry no signal.kind on the census product basis; origin is contracted by R-OBS-CONT-PROVENANCE.
No k6/Project-81 resource or trace marker exists, so this row’s traffic cannot be separated from organic fleet traffic in a later census.

redaction.rule: Delegate task material is published only as a digest, a length and the delegate mode, inside a public-safe Tempo projection. Task text, the child-minted token, prompt bodies, raw nonces, raw session keys, and gateway tokens never enter the artifact.

controls.positive: The delegate child, bound through the child observer, schedules its own nonce-bound continue_work, wakes on hop 2 with CHILD-HOP2-DONE, and the parent reproduces the child-minted token in a later run.
controls.negative: A harness prompt echo, or the parent’s own continue_delegate task text, cannot satisfy the parent-return receipt; an observer/event child-identity conflict is PARTIAL.

backendUnavailable.notes: A degraded or empty Tempo answer leaves tempo-trace-json and its correlation receipt pending. That is review debt, not evidence that the continuation did not happen, and it never changes the VU verdict.

verdictAuthority.pass: delegate-accepted, child-continue-work-accepted, child-hop-2-woke, and parent-return from the child’s and parent’s own transcripts. Behavioral only; the trace receipts decide review completeness, not the verdict.
verdictAuthority.partial: Any of those receipts is missing, the child is not bound, or the observer and event paths disagree. A missing or degraded trace keeps the row review-pending without changing its class.
verdictAuthority.fail: Not emitted by this scenario: an incomplete run is PARTIAL-candidate. Neither trace receipt can produce or clear a FAIL.

execution.deterministicK6: r-cw-delegate-self-continuation.js fires continue_delegate whose task makes the child call continue_work, and records the task fingerprint.
execution.manual: Manual Tempo review confirms the child’s work/fire spans; it cannot join them to the parent dispatch.
execution.relationship: The deterministic row owns the verdict. The Tempo trace receipts decide only whether review is complete; manual review corroborates topology and never upgrades a missing receipt.

liveRunSafety.notes: Delegate self-continuation row. Prefer OPENCLAW_CREATE_DISPOSABLE_SESSION=true for repeatability. Serialize per session (sameSessionConcurrencySafe=false). Ignore [k6-proof-harness] prompt echo; only post-dispatch evidence counts. PASS requires explicit post-dispatch CHILD-CW-SCHEDULED, CHILD-HOP2-DONE, and parent-return evidence; otherwise fold as PARTIAL-candidate. Since #570 the row requires two of three separate receipts: hop 2 ran (child transcript) and the child's return reached the parent (child-minted token reproduced by the parent); it does not claim that hop-2 OUTPUT reached the parent (only the turn-1 return is delivered, before hop 2). Retained PASS receipts from before #570 (2026-07-17 to 2026-08-25) are historically non-discriminating: their parent-stream substring checks could be satisfied by the parent's own continue_delegate task text (plausible, not proven); they are not re-classified as FAIL.
